Business History: A Resource Guide

General Works

Listed here are print resources that can be used to either look up individual companies and their histories or identify sources of historical business information. The following materials link to fuller bibliographic information in the Library of Congress Online Catalog . Links to digital content are provided when available.
* Business Founding Date Directory. Alphabetical and Chronological Sections. by Etna M. Kelley
Call Number: HD2785 .K4
Published/Created: [1954]
The main volume lists almost 10,000 businesses founded in the United States between 1687 and 1915, arranged alphabetically by company name and chronologically by founding date.

Catalogs Versus Databases

Claire Nickerson
In chapter nine, you learned about library catalogs . If you ask a computer scientist, they will tell you that the library catalog is a type of database, because it stores data in a structured way. However, if you ask a librarian, they will tell you that a library catalog and a library database are two different things, although there is some overlap in how they function. Here’s a comparison:
* Library Catalog | Library Database
* * Tells you where to find items, either on a shelf or in a database. It provides the equivalent of a street address, but it doesn’t store the full text of an item. | * St

...

* * Is designed to list all of the resources a library has available | * Is designed to list a subset of the resources a library has available, usually focusing on a specific subject (e.g.

...

It can be hard to tell by looking whether a search tool is a catalog or a database, since both may use similar search interfaces. Here are some clues to look for:
* Can you search directly from the library’s homepage? It’s probably a catalog or omnibus search tool. Do you have to click through several other pages to get to the search interface?

...

, do the results include physical items (such as printed books) and their call numbers ? It’s definitely a catalog. Can you access the full, digital text of articles or e-books without going to another web address? It’s definitely a database.
In summary:
* Catalog | Database
